docs.title: Pet API Guide
docs.text:
Complete Developer Reference and Integration Manual

🐾 Petstore API · v3.0 · petstore3.swagger.io/api/v3

The Petstore Pet API provides a RESTful interface to manage pet records in the store. It supports full CRUD operations, allowing you to create, retrieve, update, and delete pet entries using standard HTTP methods.

This guide is designed for:

  • 👩‍💻 Developers integrating with the API programmatically
  • 🔗 Integration Teams building connected services
  • 🛒 End Customers exploring platform capabilities
  • 🧪 QA Engineers validating endpoint behavior

docs.title: Add a New Pet
docs.text:
POST /pet

Adds a new pet record to the store. The request body must contain the pet's name and at least one photo URL. Returns the created pet object on success.

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text:
application/json
{
  "id": 12345,
  "name": "Rover",
  "category": { "id": 1, "name": "Dogs" },
  "photoUrls": ["https://example.com/rover.jpg"],
  "tags": [{ "id": 1, "name": "friendly" }],
  "status": "available"
}

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
Status Meaning Notes 200 OK Pet added successfully Returns the pet object 400 Invalid input Check required fields

→ Update an Existing Pet (PUT /pet)

docs.title: Delete a Pet
docs.text:
DELETE /pet/{petId}

Permanently removes a pet record from the store by its ID. An optional api_key header can be passed for authorization purposes.

docs.title: Path Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Required Description petId integer (int64) Required ID of the pet to delete

docs.title: Header Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Required Description api_key string Optional API key for authorization

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text:
DELETE /pet/12345
api_key: special-key

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
Status Meaning 200 OK Pet deleted successfully 400 Invalid pet ID supplied 404 Pet not found

→ Endpoint Summary

docs.title: Find Pet by ID
docs.text:
GET /pet/{petId}

Retrieves a single pet by its unique numeric ID.

docs.title: Path Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Required Description petId integer (int64) Required Unique ID of the pet to retrieve

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text: GET /pet/12345

docs.title: Example Response (200 OK)
docs.text:
{
  "id": 12345,
  "name": "Rover",
  "category": { "id": 1, "name": "Dogs" },
  "photoUrls": ["https://example.com/rover.jpg"],
  "tags": [{ "id": 1, "name": "friendly" }],
  "status": "available"
}

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
Status Meaning 200 OK Successful. Returns the pet object. 400 Invalid ID supplied. The ID must be a positive integer. 404 Pet not found

→ Update Pet with Form Data (POST)

docs.title: Find Pets by Status
docs.text:
GET /pet/findByStatus

Returns pets filtered by their availability status. Multiple statuses can be supplied.

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Required Description status string (enum) Optional Filter by status: available, pending, sold

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text: GET /pet/findByStatus?status=available

docs.title: Example Response (200 OK)
docs.text:
[
  {
    "id": 12345,
    "name": "Rover",
    "status": "available",
    "photoUrls": ["https://example.com/rover.jpg"]
  },
  {
    "id": 67890,
    "name": "Bella",
    "status": "available",
    "photoUrls": ["https://example.com/bella.jpg"]
  }
]

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
Status Meaning 200 OK Successful. Returns an array of pets. 400 Invalid status value supplied

→ Find Pets by Tags (GET)

docs.title: Find Pets by Tags
docs.text:
GET /pet/findByTags

Returns pets that match one or more specified tags. Tag values are passed as repeated query parameters.

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Required Description tags array[string] Required One or more tag names to filter by

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text: GET /pet/findByTags?tags=friendly&tags=energetic

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
Status Meaning 200 OK Successful. Returns an array of matching pets. 400 Invalid tag value supplied

→ Find Pet by ID (GET)

docs.title: Update Pet with Form Data
docs.text:
POST /pet/{petId}

Updates an existing pet's name or status using URL-encoded form data rather than a JSON body.

docs.title: Path Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Required Description petId integer (int64) Required ID of the pet to update

docs.title: Form Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Required Description name string Optional Updated name of the pet status string Optional Updated status: available, pending, sold

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text:
POST /pet/12345
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

name=Rover+Jr&status=pending

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
Status Meaning 200 OK Pet updated successfully 405 Invalid input. The form data failed validation.

→ Delete a Pet (DELETE)

docs.title: Update an Existing Pet
docs.text:
PUT /pet

Updates an existing pet's data. The id field in the request body must match an existing pet record.

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text:
application/json
{
  "id": 12345,
  "name": "Rover Updated",
  "category": { "id": 1, "name": "Dogs" },
  "photoUrls": ["https://example.com/rover2.jpg"],
  "tags": [{ "id": 2, "name": "energetic" }],
  "status": "sold"
}

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
Status Meaning Notes 200 OK Pet updated successfully Returns updated pet object 400 Invalid ID supplied Verify the pet ID is a valid integer 404 Pet not found No pet matches the given ID 405 Validation exception Data failed server-side validation

→ Find Pets by Status (GET)

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Certain endpoints (such as DELETE /pet/{petId}) accept an optional api_key header for authorization. While the Petstore demo environment does not enforce authentication on most routes, production deployments should use the OAuth 2.0 or API Key mechanisms described in the following table.

Auth Type Header / Field Example API Key api_key (header) api_key: special-key OAuth 2.0 Authorization (header) Bearer <token>

Note

Most read endpoints (GET) in this guide do not require authentication. Write and delete operations may require an API key in production environments even though the public demo does not enforce it.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Petstore Pet API provides a RESTful interface to manage pet records in the store. It supports full CRUD operations, allowing you to create, retrieve, update, and delete pet entries using standard HTTP methods. This guide is designed for both end customers exploring the capabilities of the platform and developers integrating with it programmatically.

Base URL

All API requests must be prefixed with the following base URL.

https://petstore3.swagger.io/api/v3

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text:
Method Capability GET Retrieve pet data POST Create a new pet PUT Update pet info DELETE Remove a pet record

Continue to Authentication to learn how requests are secured.

docs.title: Request and Response Format
docs.text:
All request and response bodies use JSON (preferred) or XML. Include the appropriate Content-Type and Accept headers with each request.

Content-Type: application/json
Accept:       application/json

All endpoint examples in this guide use JSON. If you need XML support, set the Content-Type and Accept headers to application/xml instead.

docs.title: Pet Data Model
docs.text:
The following describes the full Pet object returned or accepted by the API.

Field Type Required Description id integer (int64) Optional Unique identifier for the pet name string Required Name of the pet (e.g., "Rover") category object Optional Category object: { id, name } photoUrls array[string] Required List of photo URLs for the pet tags array[object] Optional List of tag objects: [ { id, name } ] status string (enum) Optional Pet availability: available | pending | sold

docs.title: Full Schema Example
docs.text:
{
  "id": 12345,
  "name": "Rover",
  "category": {
    "id": 1,
    "name": "Dogs"
  },
  "photoUrls": [
    "https://example.com/photos/rover_main.jpg"
  ],
  "tags": [
    { "id": 1, "name": "friendly" },
    { "id": 2, "name": "trained" }
  ],
  "status": "available"
}

Need help?

Visit the interactive Swagger UI at petstore3.swagger.io to test endpoints live in your browser.

docs.title: HTTP Status Code Reference
docs.text: Code Name Description 200 OK Request succeeded. Response body contains the result. 400 Bad Request Invalid input. The request syntax is malformed or required fields are missing. 404 Not Found The requested resource (pet) does not exist. 405 Method Not Allowed HTTP method is not supported for this endpoint.
